sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Spider Solitaire is a solitaire card game that requires players to create eight sequences of cards from King to Ace in the same suit. The game starts with a tableau of seven columns, with the top card in each column face up and the rest face down. The remaining cards are placed in a stock pile, which can be drawn from to create new sequences. The goal is to move all the cards to the foundation piles, which are located at the top-right corner of the tableau.

The game's mechanics are simple yet challenging. Players can move cards from the tableau to the foundation piles or to other cards in the same suit in descending order (King to Ace). Cards can also be moved from the stock pile to the foundation piles or to the tableau. The game offers a unique challenge as players must think strategically to move cards around and create sequences. The game also features a undo feature, allowing players to correct their moves and try again.

One of the key aspects of Spider Solitaire is its flexibility. Players can choose the number of suits they wish to play with, which affects the difficulty level of the game. Playing with fewer suits means that players have to think more strategically to move cards around and create sequences. The game also features a timer, which adds an extra layer of challenge for players who enjoy a sense of urgency. Overall, the core gameplay mechanics of Spider Solitaire make it an engaging and challenging puzzle game that is perfect for players of all skill levels.
